brief: An octagonal hinged wooden box, its lid open, packed tight with workshop hardware in a sailor's-valentine radial rosette. There are brass screws, galvanised washers, copper rivets, hex nuts and coiled springs, all sorted in concentric rings around a central compass-rose of red-handled fuses. Each piece is rendered hyperreal through meticulous pen stippling and then washed with thin sienna, brass-yellow and verdigris watercolour. Oily fingerprints smudge the glass of the lid, which is propped open at an angle. The scene is warm, cluttered and obsessively ordered.

Seen from directly above, eight skydivers link hands in a star formation over a dark indigo-blue void. They are arranged like the repeating embroidered flying figures of a Paracas mantle. Each figure is hyperreal: rippling jumpsuits in madder red, ochre gold and olive, wind-pinned goggles, straining fingers, altimeter straps. Their colours rotate from figure to figure the way textile figures alternate. Model the forms with dense, tight, stitch-like hatching. The ground is solid, deep and matte with tiny cloud wisps far below. The overall rhythm is a strict repeating grid that breathes with the figures' movement.

A girl in a red gingham sundress sits on white painted porch steps, biting into buttered corn on the cob. She is rendered with Kodachrome saturation: lipstick reds, hard cyan sky, egg-yolk kernels and deep near-black shadows under the step treads. Use watercolour laid in strong, glassy, non-muddy glazes, keeping the colour dense and clean. Buttery highlights and kernel skins are hyper-detailed. A crisp white cardboard slide-mount border surrounds the image, with a tiny typed date stamp. The late-afternoon sun is low and warm, with long blue shadows.

A polished stainless soup ladle hangs on a hook and fills the frame. Its convex bowl holds a fisheye reflection of a busy diner: a cook's white apron, red vinyl stools, fluorescent tubes and a window bending into arcs. Render it in full colour with saturated marker blends. Contrast is extreme, running from pure white specular slashes to inky near-black, with hard-edged reflections that warp and pinch at the rim. Fine brushed-steel scratches run along the handle. The real background is blurred beige tile, so the reflected world is sharper than the actual one.

A luchador stands in full regalia, masked, caped and belted with chrome buckles, sequinned and feathered. He fills a tall, narrow vertical slab in the frontal, crowded composition of a Maya stele. Every sequin, laced boot and stitched mask seam is hyperreal, but the whole is toned like carved limestone: grey-ochre charcoal mass with sanguine wash. Strong raking light from the upper left gives deep shadowed undercuts. The background is packed with blocky glyph panels and a weathered, pitted stone texture with lichen flecks.

The worn sole of a skate shoe fills the page edge to edge, as if pressed onto a photocopier glass. It is rendered in brutal black toner, with every tread groove, embedded pebble, chewing-gum scar and frayed canvas edge hyperreal. Midtones collapse into gritty speckle and streaky drum banding from heavy spray grain. Highlights are blown to raw paper white. A strip of torn masking tape and a crooked cut-and-paste typed caption sit at the corner. There is one cheap overprint of fluorescent orange, slightly misregistered.

A single unbroken lemon peel hangs from the tip of a paring knife and spirals down a deep Norwegian blue-green ground. Every turn of the peel follows the swelling C- and S-scrolls of rosemaling. The rind is built from tapering liner-brush strokes that start fat and flick to hairlines, the way rosemaling leaves are laid. The zest is cadmium yellow with oily pore dimples picked out in pale cream, and the pith underside is chalky ivory with fibrous threads. A thin margin of soft vermilion acanthus flourishes curls at the corners, painted with the same confident single strokes. The light is warm and even, and each strip carries a glossy specular ridge.

A red onion is halved and its rings are shown as a stack of offset translucent sheets. Each concentric layer is drawn on its own pale vellum-like wash and shifted slightly out of register, so ghost outlines of the previous ring peek through. Use coloured pencil: magenta and violet skins grading to wet white flesh, with glistening cell texture and moist highlights. Pale grey registration crosses and faint pencil construction lines sit at the margins. The sheets build up into a soft milky haze at the edges, while the central cut stays sharp and juicy. The ground is a cool drafting-table off-white.

A wedge of sponge cake sits on a saucer, wrapped tight in crumpled cling film. The plastic creases catch flashes of opal play-of-colour: sudden patches of electric green, flame orange and lilac, floating in a milky translucent haze. Paint it in watercolour, with soft milk-white veils over pale buttercream and the crumb visible but blurred beneath the film. Then set sharp, broken spectral flecks along each fold with a fine spray and stipple, so the colour seems to shift as you look. The background is a dull kitchen counter in oatmeal laminate. Air bubbles and stretched wrinkles stay hyper-precise.

A heap of ripe raspberries tumbles from a punnet across the full frame, every drupelet rendered as a bandhani tie-dye dot. Each is a rounded madder-red bead with a tiny white resist core where the highlight sits, plus a faint dye halo bleeding into the next. Build the berries from dense spray stippling and small watercolour dabs, varying from crimson through deep wine to unripe coral. Fine hairs catch the light as thin silver pen strokes. The punnet is green, translucent and moulded. The light is soft and directional, with rich cast shadows between berries.

Three thick watermelon wedges lie fanned on a dark tabletop. Their structure is translated into Guna mola reverse appliqué: rind, white pith, pink flesh and seeds become nested contour bands, each echoed by thin channels of contrasting colour, as if layers of cloth were cut back to reveal the ones below. The fills are flat bold marker in leaf green, chalk white, watermelon red and jet black. Each fill carries hyperreal juice beads, a sugary crystalline grain and wet seed gloss. Crisp outlines are slightly uneven, like hand stitching. The background is deep orange with echoing slits.

A pet tortoise is drawn huge on brown kraft cardboard, every scute and wrinkle recorded with obsessive outsider-art compulsion. Each shell plate is filled with concentric growth rings in waxy crayon, ochre, umber and olive, pressed hard so it shines. Its leathery neck is covered in hundreds of tiny felt-tip scales, each individually outlined. The tortoise is uncannily accurate, but placed with naïve flatness and a wobbly hand-ruled border. The dense surrounding ground is filled with repeated lettuce leaves and dandelions. The cardboard grain shows through everywhere.

Seen from directly overhead, a banana leaf holds a neat grid of string hoppers (idiyappam). Each nest of steamed rice noodles is drawn as a continuous looping white line in the manner of a kolam: one unbroken thread circling a central point and returning to itself. Draw them in fine white pen over a deep glossy green watercolour leaf, with its parallel veins and tears exact. Steam beads and translucent noodle edges catch the light. A small dish of coconut sambol sits off-centre in coral-pink. Everything is orderly and meditative, yet edible-real.

An open cardboard egg carton holds one cracked egg, its yolk slumped and still glossy. It is drawn in graphite and soft charcoal on a ground of pewter-grey wash. The image should feel like a mirror-silver plate: the tones are silvery and slightly reversed in the highlights, the moulded pulp fibres are rendered grain by grain, and the depth of field is shallow. Around the oval mat edge, tarnish blooms in iridescent peacock blue, bronze and rose, applied as soft stained halos. A faint gilt brass mat frame encloses everything. The only near-colour is a dim, desaturated yolk amber.

Seen straight down, a white enamel mug of black coffee sits on top of a juddering washing machine. Its surface is locked into a standing-wave pattern of concentric rings and petal-like nodes. The drawing is fine-pen engraving: dense concentric hatching for the dark liquid, with ring crests left as white paper and thin crescents of tan crema at the rim, touched with amber marker. The machine's white lid fills the rest of the frame with stippled brushed-steel texture and a stray sock edge. The image is graphic, symmetrical and hypnotic, yet every reflection on the meniscus is exact.

An elderly woman in a floral housecoat leans against a raw board-marked concrete wall, filling the frame from the side. The wall dominates. Charcoal mass and directional hatching carve the timber-plank impressions, the grain ridges, round tie-holes and grey lime bleed lines in cool ash tones. Her face and hands are rendered with the same unsentimental granular detail: wrinkles like poured seams and age spots like aggregate. The only colour is a faded cerise in her housecoat roses. Flat overcast light casts no drama. The mood is stoic, monumental and quietly humane.

A wooden honey dipper is held aloft against a backlit window. A long ribbon of honey stretches, folds and pools onto a stack of pancakes below. The honey is built in many glassy watercolour glazes of amber, burnt orange and pale gold, with satin-smooth gradients and razor-white specular streaks. Internal light glows through the thickest folds. The dipper's ridges and the pancake crumb are rendered in fine coloured pencil. The window beyond is a soft cream blur. The surfaces feel pulled, taut and translucent like spun confection, frozen at the instant before the ribbon snaps.

An extreme close-up of parted lips under blown-out beauty-dish lighting, almost entirely white. Hard graphite pencil does nearly all the work in a whisper-thin tonal range: pale silver-grey for the lip lines, a single deep graphite crease at the corner of the mouth. A faint watercolour bloom of rose madder sits only in the lower lip's gloss pool. The pool's highlight is left as pure untouched paper, edged so cleanly it reads as wet lacquer. Fine down hair and skin pores fade out where the overexposure eats the edges. The image is airy, clinical and expensive, like a cosmetics print holding its breath.

A tight crop of a hand with long almond-shaped chrome-powder nails gripping a pearlescent lilac flip phone, rendered as an airbrushed late-nineties ad. Soft spray gradients carry ice blue, periwinkle and liquid silver. Hard white specular streaks are laid with crisp marker over the gradients. Every reflective surface holds a warped fisheye studio: a softbox, a blurred face, a lens flare. Cuticles, knuckle creases and a tiny chip at one nail tip are drawn in hairline pen with clinical precision. The background is a frosted cyan haze with floating bubble glints. The finish is glossy, toy-like and seductive, slick beyond belief.

A packed, frontal view of a jeepney windscreen and dashboard, filling every inch. A rosary and fringed tassels swing from the mirror. A row of chrome horse figurines, stickers of saints, plastic flowers and a coin tray full of pesos crowd below. Flat, saturated marker fills in candy red, lemon, kelly green and electric blue sit next to hairline pen pinstripes and scrolling borders. The chrome gets sharp white-and-ink zigzag reflections. Hard tropical noon floods through the glass, and the street beyond is a hot washed-out blur. The mood is loud, devotional and maximal, with no breathing room, precise down to scuffed vinyl stitching.
